title: Predictive weight loader and KV snapshot preload for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: reduce cold-start latency and variability for Dedicated GPU pools by combining a predictive model-weight streaming service with KV cache snapshot preload and lightweight in-memory checks. This ticket implements a deployable staging mechanism that streams partial weight shards, applies fast delta patches, and preloads per-route KV snapshots into a warm tier to meet throughput guarantees without maintaining full hot capacity across all nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Mean cold-start latency for 95th percentile requests on dedicated pools decreases by >= 40% compared to baseline (measured across three representative workloads)
End-to-end rollout with canary on 10% of fleet runs for 48 hours with no increased error rate and stable memory footprints
KV preload mechanism can restore a route-specific KV snapshot within <= 150ms on pod resume (measured median)
Predictive loader accuracy: top-3 predicted model shards to load contain the actual shards used in 90% of traced requests during 30m traffic windows
No regression in steady-state throughput (RPS) or token-per-second GPU utilization beyond +/-5% after enabling streaming preload
Operational metrics: new instrumentation (weight_stream_ops, kv_snapshot_hits, partial_load_evictions) are populating Console dashboards and alerting thresholds are configured
tasks: Design and document slice-based weight streaming protocol (binary-compatible with current model artifacts)
Implement weight loader worker that supports prioritized shard streaming and delta patch applying
Build KV snapshotter service capable of producing compressed snapshots per route and a lightweight bloom-filter index
Integrate loader with autoscaler: expose preload readiness signal and optional pre-provisioning hook
Add metrics (histograms and counters) and tracing spans for weight streaming and KV apply paths
Create canary deployment plan and runbook with rollback criteria
Write e2e tests (integration env) that simulate pod resurrection under typical workload distributions
Update documentation: API flags for enabling predictive preload and cost estimation guidance
updates: 2026-02-10 - Asha created the ticket and pitched high-level approach: slice streaming + KV snapshots. Assigned to Liam.
2026-02-18 - Proto: defined shard format and small POC streaming prototype shows median shard apply time ~80ms for 1GB model split into 32 slices.
2026-02-26 - Decided to use bloom-filter pre-checks to avoid loading cold shards for low-probability routes (trade-off: additional memory for filters).
2026-03-04 - Implemented basic KV snapshot export and bloom index. Local tests show kv snapshot restore median 110ms for ~2k keys compressed with zstd.
2026-03-09 - Integrated preload readiness signal with autoscaler; small flakiness observed under bursty traffic (investigating backpressure path).
2026-03-12 - Canary scheduled for 2026-03-18 on staging fleet. Runbook prepared and alert thresholds proposed.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full persistent hot pool vs. predictive partial warm start. Chosen approach reduces idle GPU memory costs at expense of increased complexity during load path.
We will prioritize routes by recent heatmaps (last-1h) and use half-life decay to avoid thrashing after traffic spikes.
Delta patching uses chunked checksums so we can apply only changed segments when model variants are minor (helps with model rollouts).
KV snapshots will be sharded by route and compressed; snapshot index stored in metadata service with TTL and LRU eviction policy.
Fallback behavior: if a preload fails or is slow, system falls back to cold-load + degraded concurrency limit and signals autoscaler to spin up extra capacity.

Cost estimate: initial canary expected ~120 GPU-hours for integration and validation; projected steady-state savings depend on hit-rate but estimated 18-25% reduction in reserved hot GPUs for typical enterprise workload mix.
